items.summary: Proto types in encounter service.go Input/Output types (not just orchestrator.go)
items.details: orchestrators/encounter/service.go:7 imports pb and uses pb.MonsterType in MonsterCombatState (line 459), pb.CombatAbilityId in ActivateCombatAbilityInput (line 511), and pb.ActionId in ExecuteActionInput (line 535). The first reviewer pass noted proto types in the orchestrator implementation (~50 pb. refs in orchestrator.go), but the Input/Output types in service.go are also contaminated. Any caller of the Service interface must also import pb.

items.summary: entities package imports and constructs proto messages
items.details: entities/entity_state.go and entities/encounter_state_builder.go contain full proto construction functions (ToEntityStateProto, BuildEncounterStateData, CombatStateToProto). These belong in the handler converter layer. entities/encounter_events.go embeds *dnd5ev1alpha1.EncounterStateData, *dnd5ev1alpha1.EntityState, *dnd5ev1alpha1.CombatState as json:"-" fields in 9 event structs. entities/room.go stores apiv1alpha1.GridType (a proto enum) directly on the Room entity struct.

items.summary: RoomData stored as interface{} in EncounterData and input types
items.details: encounters/repository.go: EncounterData.RoomData, SaveInput.RoomData, and UpdateInput.RoomData are all typed as interface{} with a comment 'Temporarily using interface{} until spatial is fixed'. The orchestrator uses type assertions at every access point. This makes the repository and orchestrator brittle and disables type checking for room data.

items.summary: DEPRECATED fields in EncounterData still present during migration
items.details: encounters/repository.go: EncounterData has both Monsters []*monster.Data + CharacterHP map[string]int (DEPRECATED comments) AND Entities map[string]*entities.EntityStateData (the new unified approach). Both are present simultaneously. There is no migration path or deprecation deadline visible.

items.summary: SandboxRoom service has interface but no implementation wired
items.details: services/sandboxroom/service.go defines a Service interface with 11 methods covering room generation, spatial queries, and entity management. There is no orchestrator, handler, or server wiring for this service. It is a declared interface with no implementation path visible.

items.summary: Three Position types with different int/float64 signatures
items.details: entities.Position uses float64 X,Y,Z. dungeon.Position uses int X,Y,Z. apiv1alpha1.Position (proto) uses float64 X,Y,Z. RoomOrigins in entities.Dungeon stores dungeon.Position (int). Entity positions in EncounterData use entities.Position (float64). The int/float64 mismatch requires type casts at every boundary. This is the root cause of the five coordinate-space bugs.

items.summary: dungeon_mapper.go line 44 routes crypt theme to ThemeDebugWalls
items.details: mapTheme in dungeon_mapper.go: case 'crypt' returns dungeon.ThemeDebugWalls with a TODO comment 'swap back to ThemeCrypt after wall UI testing'. This is present in the docs/honest-status-snapshot branch. All crypt dungeons show debug walls in any build from this branch.

items.summary: OpenDoor reveal stores room-B walls and entities without translating from room-local to dungeon-absolute, so revealed rooms overlap room A geometrically
items.delta: Localized to buildRoomLayoutProto in orchestrator.go (line ~1098). Entity positions and CubeEntities were already translated correctly; only RoomLayout.walls in EncounterStateData.rooms were room-local. Fix on branch fix/cross-room-state-wave2 applies origin element-wise to each wall vertex at the producer. Awaiting Kirk's playtest verification before flipping to resolved.

items.summary: Wall-collision / event-publish consumers loaded only currentRoom.Walls, missing every other revealed room's perimeter walls
items.delta: Sibling of #493: that bug was at the producer (rendering data); this one was at the consumers (collision + event data). MoveCharacter, executeMonsterTurns, ResolveAttack, executeMoveAction all loaded dungeon.GetRoom(currentRoomID).Walls and treated that as the encounter wall set. After OpenDoor revealed room B, room B's perimeter was invisible — collision passed straight through. New helper loadAbsoluteWallsForRevealedRooms (revealed_walls.go) returns the union in dungeon-absolute. Wall consumers now use this. MoveCharacter / executeMoveAction also stop translating target absolute → room-local before the wall check (consistent absolute-frame collision). executeMonsterTurns drops the per-step localToAbsoluteOrLocal on turnResult.Movement (absolute in, absolute out). Commit 44ce47f layered onto branch fix/cross-room-state-wave2. Awaiting Kirk's playtest verification.

items.summary: Player-move events appear to never reach the web client visually; investigation pinpoints fix is web-side, API publish path is intact
items.delta: Bug reported on Wave 2 playtest (and confirmed on main, not a Wave 2 regression). MoveCharacter accepts the request and returns success. Monster pathing/attack/death events DO arrive on the client. Player-move events visibly do not move the character. Traced the publish chain end-to-end: orchestrator.go:1846 publishes MovementCompletedEvent with UpdatedEntity (built from encOutput.Data.Entities[entityID] at line 1803-1819) and CombatStateProto (always built). entities/encounter_events_json.go:261-297 wraps these json:"-" proto fields in a base64/proto-wire-format MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON shim so they survive Redis pub/sub. handler.go:948-955 maps both fields to the proto MovementCompletedEvent that ships to the client. New regression tests verify each link: TestPublishSubscribe_MovementCompleted_PreservesProtoFields (publisher-level Redis roundtrip with miniredis) and TestMoveCharacter_PublishesEventWithUpdatedEntityAndCombatState (orchestrator publishes with UpdatedEntity and CombatStateProto when Entities map is populated). Both pass. Compared to monster events: MonsterTurnCompletedEvent has Movement []dungeon.AbsolutePosition (json:"movement", JSON-preserved) which the web client uses in applyMonsterMovement (LobbyView.tsx:89-114) to update room.entities[monsterId].position. Player movement has the symmetric proto field — MovementCompletedEvent.path (handler.go:940-947 builds from FinalPosition, also JSON-preserved) — but the web client's handleMovementCompleted (LobbyView.tsx:691-706) does NOT consume event.path. It only updates state when event.updatedEntity or event.combatState is truthy. So if the API publishes correctly but updatedEntity is degraded for any reason (e.g., Entities map missing the player at move time), the player visibly stays put. Fix is on the web side: handleMovementCompleted should fall back to event.path for the entity-position update, mirroring what applyMonsterMovement does for monsters. No rpg-api code change needed; regression tests added on branch fix/cross-room-state-wave2 to pin the publish-path contract.
